title: Main-form lock during script prompts hinges on the magic control name "btnStopAll" and silently no-ops if it's missing
existing_state: While a script prompt (input/choose/confirm/etc.) is open, MainFormPromptLock disables the entire main form except the ancestor chain of a control found by name probe: `FindControlByName(mainForm, "btnStopAll")` (Services/Scripting/Commands/ScriptPromptDialogRunner.cs:384). If that probe fails — control renamed, moved into a different container type, or replaced by a toolbar item — `TryAcquire` returns null (379-386) and the prompt runs with no lock at all: the user can freely edit the host grid, change environments, or start another run mid-prompt, with no error or log to indicate the protection vanished. A Form1 designer rename is exactly the kind of change that would never be connected to "script prompts stopped locking the UI" in review.
recommendation: Replace the name probe with an explicit injection point: Form1 already feeds ScriptPromptDialogRunner configuration (DefaultPromptFontSize, AnchorFormOverride at lines 16-26) — add a `StopControlProvider` (Func<Control?>) the form sets once at startup, and Debug.Fail/log when it yields nothing so a broken wiring is loud in dev instead of silent in prod.
user_benefit: Removes a one-string coupling between the scripting layer and Form1's control tree that can silently disable a safety behavior (UI locked during prompts) after an unrelated UI refactor.

evidence.note: TryAcquire returns null (no lock, no warning) when the literal name "btnStopAll" is not found
